name: Supplier Credit Risk Monitor
goal: Monitor supplier credit risk from news: search recent news for each supplier, extract distress signals, score each supplier against a distress rubric, and produce an alert list plus a monitoring briefing.

tasks.name: collect_news
tasks.description: Search recent news for each supplier being monitored.

inputs.name: lookback_days
inputs.description: How many days back to search, e.g. 14

outputs.name: news_digest
outputs.description: Dated, sourced news items grouped by supplier

tasks.prompt:
Monitor these suppliers: {suppliers}
Look back {lookback_days} days.

For each supplier run several ddgs_search queries, for example:
- "<supplier> credit rating"
- "<supplier> bankruptcy OR default OR restructuring"
- "<supplier> financial results profit warning"
- "<supplier> strike OR layoffs OR plant closure"

Prefer financial press, rating-agency statements, exchange filings and official notices.

Return a digest grouped by supplier. For every item give: date, headline, one-line summary, publisher, URL. Drop promotional, duplicated or off-topic results. If a supplier has nothing material, write "no material news".
tasks.system_prompt: You are a supply-chain credit analyst collecting evidence, not opinions. Only report items you actually retrieved, always with date and URL.

tasks.name: extract_signals
tasks.description: Turn the raw news digest into structured distress signals per supplier.

inputs.name: news_digest
inputs.description: Dated, sourced news items grouped by supplier

outputs.name: signals
outputs.description: Distress signals per supplier, most severe first

tasks.prompt:
From the news digest below, extract only items that could signal supplier distress — financial, operational, legal, governance or supply-continuity.

Digest:
{news_digest}

For each signal output one line:
supplier | signal_type | date | severity (critical/high/medium/low) | one-sentence evidence | source URL

Group by supplier, most severe first. Discard anything that is not about the supplier itself. If a supplier has no signals, list it once with "no signals".
tasks.system_prompt: You extract verifiable signals from evidence. Never invent an item, date or URL that is not in the digest.

tasks.name: score_supplier_risk
tasks.description: Grade each supplier's credit risk against the distress rubric.

outputs.name: risk_scores
outputs.description: Per-supplier tier, score, drivers and confidence

tasks.prompt:
Score each supplier's credit risk using the rubric in your system prompt.

Signals:
{signals}

For each supplier output:
supplier | tier (critical/high/medium/low) | score 0-100 | key drivers | evidence cited with URLs | confidence (high/medium/low) | what would change the tier

Be explicit when evidence is thin or stale, and never let a single unverified article push a supplier to critical.
tasks.system_prompt: You are a credit-risk officer applying a fixed rubric consistently across suppliers.

tasks.name: flag_alerts
tasks.description: Produce the actionable alert list for the risk team.

outputs.name: alerts
outputs.description: Suppliers needing attention with trigger and recommended action

tasks.prompt:
Produce the alert list for the risk team.

Risk scores:
{risk_scores}

Signals:
{signals}

Output one block per supplier that needs attention where:
(1) the supplier is tiered critical or high, or
(2) any single critical-severity signal is present, whatever the tier.

Each block: supplier, trigger, why it matters for supply continuity, evidence URL, recommended immediate action, and an owner-type (procurement / finance / legal). Order by severity. If nothing qualifies, output exactly "No alerts".
tasks.system_prompt: You are the credit-risk analyst deciding what interrupts the team's week. Be precise and do not cry wolf.

tasks.name: draft_report
tasks.description: Write the periodic supplier monitoring briefing.

inputs.name: news_digest
inputs.description: Dated, sourced news items grouped by supplier

tasks.prompt:
Write the supplier credit-risk monitoring briefing.

Risk scores:
{risk_scores}

News digest:
{news_digest}

Structure:
1. Run summary — suppliers monitored and count per tier.
2. Tier changes and what caused them.
3. Supplier-by-supplier assessment with evidence and URLs.
4. Watch list and leading indicators to re-check next period.
5. Data gaps and confidence limits.

Every claim must trace to a cited item in the digest; do not speculate beyond the evidence.
tasks.system_prompt: You write factual analyst briefings for a procurement and finance audience. Plain language, no filler.
